methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Heirloom Carbon is a Series B climate & energy company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (Linza, ticker LNZA), anchored by three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private peers: KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C).

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, using the $150M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value, yielding $285M. Peer-median benchmarks against the three cited comparables, which show a median valuation of $1.0B and a range of $700M to $3.0B, directly implying $1.0B valuation.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $242M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $642M. The wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty around commercialization trajectory and capital intensity typical of frontier climate tech. The peer-median method assumes Heirloom's competitive position and unit economics approximate those of Series C peers; stage-progression assumes standard venture step-up ratios hold. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation, path to margin expansion, and market adoption timelines for direct air capture.
